Steam drum level control in the HRSG is crucial to ensuring the effective operation of steam systems. If the water level goes too high, water can enter the steam turbine, potentially causing damage. Conversely, if the water level drops too low, the HRSG can run dry, putting the tubes in danger. By compensating for variations in steam demands, the control sys- tem ensures that any volume of steam leaving the steam drum is promptly replaced by an equivalent quantity of water, thereby guaranteeing the stability and efficiency of the over- all steam system. In addition, a detailed physics-based model, such as the models from the ThermoPower Library, can be employed to examine the dynamic behaviors and val- 63 idate the proposed model. The ThermoPower Library (TPL) has an example model to achieve the goal of maintaining the steam drum level. This example model can be found inThermoPower.Examples.RankineCycle.Simulators.ClosedLoop.
